 The 3-2-1 Column: Panthers have a winnable game tomorrow, basketball season on the horizon and more
 Setting the stage for Pitt's home game with Georgia Tech on Saturday and the start of a new basketball season on Monday
 Jim Hammett 14 The intersection of the final stretch of the football season and the start of basketball is here and that provides plenty of storylines heading into the weekend.
 Pat Narduzzi's team breaks into the final third of its season and will look to snap a three-game losing streak when the play host to Georgia Tech under the lights on Saturday night at Acrisure Stadium.
 Jeff Capel's Panthers are set to open its new campaign on Monday night when Rider comes to Petersen Events Center. 
 Let's dig into it all in this week's 3-2-1 Column .
 THREE THINGS WE KNOW 
 If there is one to win, it's tomorrow 
 There could be a great deal to talk about what happened last weekend in Miami, but at the same time there really isn't much to say at all.  Pitt got smacked by the No. 1 team in the country, plain and simple.
 The defense couldn't contain the Hurricanes superstars. The offense was plagued by early mistakes and the special teams didn't look very good either. The Panthers committed far too many mistakes in a game where they had no room for error. Miami is really good and Pitt is not the same team it was when it started the year and the beatdown pretty much met the expectations by many going into the contest.
 This 2026 Pitt team has been trying to figure out how to navigate each week and that's why the topic at hand feels like it should be about what is ahead for the Panthers and not looking back to a blowout many saw coming.
 The actuality for this team can be acknowledged. They are undeniably affected by the loss of sophomore quarterback Mason Heintchel and his presence would have potentially changed some of the outcomes during Pitt's three-game losing streak.
 At the same time, this is now the fourth week for the Panthers under this same set of circumstances knowing that their starting quarterback is not coming back out on the field.  They have to be judged for what and who they are now. As they are nearly a month in this new reality, the expectation should be to start winning.
 The Panthers have an opportunity to do that tomorrow when Georgia Tech comes to Acrisure Stadium for a 7:30 kick on ESPN2.
 Pitt is currently favored by 7.5 points over the Yellow Jackets.  This is now the third time in four games in a post-Heintschel world where the Pitt has been been a favorite going into a game and eventually the Panthers have to get over what they lost and forge ahead with what they have.
 Pitt has plenty of its own issues that have documented quite a bit the past month, but so does Georgia Tech.  The line heading into tomorrow is largely about how they have performed to date. Brent Key's team enters this game with a 2-5 mark and having lost two straight, including a 49-27 loss to Boston College at home last week.
 Georgia Tech surrenders over 30 points and 400 yards per game on average.  The defense is missing several starters at all three levels and is coming off of a game where they allowed Boston College to rush for 399 yards a week ago.
 Offensively, Alberto Mendoza is not Haynes King and that changes the whole outlook of this team. Think back one year ago, this Georgia Tech team was ranked and King was doing a lot of the work. The Yellow Jackets ran everything through their QB in recent years and missing his mobility has cut into their rushing game as much as anything. Georgia Tech was 21st in the country in rushing in 2025 and sits at 113 in that department this season.
 The Panthers are not at full strength either, but they have some matchups they can try to favor to pull out a win.  Georgia Tech's offensive ineffectiveness has been due to an inconsistent and shuffling offensive line. 
 If Pitt can contain the run game like it normally has done this season, then getting to Mendoza could be a big factor. Georgia Tech is 114th in third-down conversions (33.7%), meaning some stops on first and second down gets this team into uncomfortable territory. The Tech quarterback is not overly mobile and the team yields 2.29 sacks per game, which is 97th nationally.
 Pitt is not having the season it wanted, nor expected. It is fair to acknowledge that when evaluating the overall performance, but the whole season can't be brushed aside under the premise of, "Well, they don't have their quarterback" either.
 There is value in not tanking down the stretch and finding a way to win some games in spite of a major loss. Perception and good energy help a great deal in college football and the vibe around Pitt following three straight losses isn't all that positive. One win doesn't cure all, but it changes the narrative for a couple days.
 Pitt has an opportunity to beat a vulnerable and struggling ACC opponent at home and get to 6-3 and head into the bye week with some good feelings and hope for the final three games. It is not unreasonable to expect that out of them tomorrow.
 Pitt QB Holden Geriner (Photo: Reuters, 247Sports) Quarterback feels less of concern this week 
 Ordinarily, a 52-23 loss would be the game where a jumbled quarterback situation gets settled. However, Holden Geriner looked mostly fine given the circumstances and his individual play answered some questions about his game overall.
 Geriner finished 18-of-32 for 268 yards and a touchdown and no interceptions.  It was not an overly inspiring stat line, but he hit on some long passes and sprinkled in some good throws agains the top-ranked team.  More importantly, Geriner seemed to make the right decisions with the ball and committed fewer mental mistakes than his previous outing.
 In Pitt's two prior losses to North Carolina and Boston College, quarterback play was a direct cause in those outcomes. The Panthers lost by four and six points, respectively, and some missed throws and poor decisions loomed large in the narrow defeats.
 Geriner did not necessarily play great against Miami, but he showed he can run an offense. That ability has value and it's something that the coaches can work with going into this week.
 The Panthers started slow against the Hurricanes with only 11 first quarter yards and did not record a first down until the second quarter. However, two of those early were stunted by penalties committed by linemen and another possession was slowed on a dropped pass from Blue Hicks.
 Once Pitt's offense and Geriner settled in, it kind of didn't matter because Miami was moving the ball at will on the other side and they were facing an uphill battle by the early parts of the second quarter.
 Geriner and Hicks appear to have a decent enough connection on deep balls. The senior quarterback also incorporated tight end Carson Kent and found Malik Knight for some nice gains. 
 The Panthers should be able to go into tomorrow's game and be able to lean on those type of reliable, veteran connections against an opposing defense ravaged by injuries.
 Geriner did not make many confident and easy reads in his first start against North Carolina, but he put the ball where it was supposed to against a pretty talented Miami team more often than not. That is why there does not feel like there was much of a quarterback debate this week.
 He will need to execute what is asked of him, but Geriner will obviously need the support of his teammates in order for Pitt to stop the bleeding with this three-game skid. It's a given his pass catchers will need to be at their best and better than they have been, but it goes beyond that.
 The Pitt offensive line has been improved from a year ago and that will obviously need to continue in both pass protection and running the ball on Saturday against a susceptible Georgia Tech defense.
 That's is clearly a bit murky at the moment with the status of running backs Ja'Kyrian Turner and Damon Ferguson up in the air, but Pitt should have some capable options to make plays if the line can establish themselves and the scheme allows for it.
 While it looks like Pitt can approach this week with some continuity at quarterback, the ability to change when its necessary has to be on the table.  Offensive Coordinator Kade Bell trusted Corey Dailey enough to start two weeks ago and Pitt has to be ready to make a change if the offense is stagnant to start the game tomorrow.
 The Panthers have to be willing and able to do what is necessary to scratch out some wins down the stretch. But for the time being, there is at least a framework around what they can do with Geriner and a path of success there as well. It is just a matter of it showing up when the lights come on tomorrow night.
 Lessons learned need to have meaning 
 The Pitt basketball team had a preseason media day of sorts earlier this week where head coach Jeff Capel spoke to the local press for the first time since the summer.  It also served as an introduction to new Panthers Naithan George, Baye Ndongo and A'lahn Sumler.
 The Panthers kick off a new season on Monday and it has been a rather quiet offseason from the program. Pitt participated in three preseason exhibitions, but two were held behind closed doors and the other was on the road at Providence.
 There were no preseason open practices for fans or even an exhibition match against a local Division II program.  When the Panthers take the court on Monday night against Rider, it will be the first time many will get to see this team whole.
 It is unclear if that was by design or just how it worked out, but the season will commence on Monday without much prior fanfare and it will kick off a pivotal year for the Panthers' coach and the program at large.
 The 2025-26 campaign ended in forgettable fashion.  Pitt posted a 13-30 record and many felt after eight seasons that Jeff Capel's time guiding the program was coming to an end.  Capel himself even indicated in some interviews throughout the offseason he believed his tenure was also on its last legs.
 As we know, that ultimately did not happen. 
 Athletic Director Allen Greene opted to bring Capel back for a ninth season. Given that the noise around his job status grew rather loud last March, this obviously is a make or break year for him personally.
 After all, Capel has only guided the Panthers to one NCAA Tournament appearance and finished with a winning record just three times over his eight years manning the sidelines at the Petersen Events Center.
 Changes were made around the embattled coach. 
 The Panthers are clearly in a higher spending bracket and that is reflected with this year's roster. Pitt is noticeably deeper than it was a season ago and it's clear they had the ammunition to make more noise in the transfer portal to bring on more credible players.
 Pitt second-year general manager Jay Kuntz was also able to involve himself and place some of his touches on the roster and this group assembled certainly brings on a lot of intrigue.
 Capel also made changes to his coaching staff and hired two popular former Pitt stars, Ricardo Greer and Ronald Ramon, to provide a new and fresh perspective off of his bench. 
 There are a lot of tools in place to make that next jump and the players on the court will have a big say in that, but the man on the sideline has to adapt as well.
 When asked what has changed about his own approach on Tuesday, Capel thought long and hard about his answer.
 "Great question," Capel said before pausing. "You know, we have two new guys on our staff. Those guys have been great. They've brought a different energy, not that any energy in the past was bad, but sometimes when you have new." 
 He also cited something that plagued last year's team and some previous seasons as well: not playing enough guys off of the bench. 
 Capel has often defaulted to a top group of players like many coaches tend to do, but high usage has led to injuries and fatigue and have worn his teams down later in the season.
 "Hopefully I can be better this year with playing more guys," said Capel. "That's something maybe we haven't done a good job of in the past. I think it helps that we have more guys that can play."
 There are more resources in place for Pitt and Capel to be successful than a season ago.  The roster has talent and upside and it will come down to how the team performs on the court, but also how the coach brings it all together.
 Capel has had a back-against-the-wall type season before, and it produced his only tournament appearance at Pitt. This year needs to follow a similar script. The lessons learned from a miserable season in 2026 will say a lot about how the 2027 campaign unfolds.
 Pitt players Naithan George, Baye Ndongo and Armani Mighty huddle up during an exhibition game at Providence (Photo: Pitt Athletics) TWO QUESTIONS WE HAVE 
 What are the biggest reasons for optimism around Pitt hoops? 
 Pitt was picked to finish 12th out of 18 in the ACC preseason poll.  The Panthers have also not gotten a lot of love by some of the preseason computer metrics and they are not necessarily showing up on many early year bracketology projections either.
 That's all very fair, of course.
 Pitt has not by synonymous with being a good basketball program of late. By their own recent results, the Panthers have plenty of work they need to do in order to earn some respect and credibility across the sport.
 However, the lowly preseason projections are not entirely indicative of the promise this team possesses.  The Panthers have the tools to outplay their projections and I think the case starts because of the floor they created with this roster.
 Senior forward Baye Ndongo has been a double-double machine for three seasons in the ACC at Georgia Tech. He is an ideal player to anchor the interior game around because he provides solid and reliable production.
 Ndongo might not average 25 points a game this season, but having a big man that can put up 12 points and 10 rebounds consistently is a good starting point for any team.
 The Panthers went heavy on the ACC familiarity trend in creating this season. Naithan George has been a three-year starter in this league, with two seasons at Georgia Tech and one at Syracuse. Jonathan Powell, Pitt's projected starting small forward, was in North Carolina rotation a year ago.
 Pitt added one of the most productive small college guards in college basketball last season in A'lahn Sumler, who led the Big South in points and assists per game for Charleston Southern.  The Panthers are taking a shot on former five-star recruit Jamil Bethea and there is optimism the Philadelphia native can finally piece it together in his third college season.
 While transfer portal additions get most of the attention these days, it also should not be discredited that Chase Foster is the highest rated player to sign with Pitt under Capel and there are hopes he can be an instant impact player in the front court.
 Aside from the more notable names on the roster, Pitt seems to have a deep array of options that can come off of the bench. Pitt has six players who are 6-9 or taller and that provides a longer list of bigger bodies than the team had at is disposal a season ago.
 The Panthers play an interesting non-conference schedule, but one that is not overly daunting either. There are some games that should test the Panthers but also other chances to score some key wins away from home in the months of November and December.
 Pitt is not going to be mistaken for a top 25 squad right now, but if enough things break their way, then this should be a team capable of getting back into the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2023.
 What are the biggest concerns surrounding Pitt hoops? 
 Many of the reasons to be optimistic are also some of the factors that also carry some doubt for Jeff Capel's team.  The Panthers are definitely centering a lot of their focus around the Ndongo and George pairing, and that alone has some people wondering about the ceiling of this team.
 Both players bring winning qualities individually, but this duo started alongside each other for two seasons at Georgia Tech and the Yellow Jackets were near the bottom of the ACC in those campaigns. The lack of success with this same nucleus elsewhere in this league certainly brings hesitation for how it will look for a third season together.
 Pitt is also entering this season with some serious question marks with its outside shooting.  The Panthers have some players who are expected to fill that void, but they seem to lack a clear go-to option in that department either. 
 Pitt was one of the worst outside shooting teams in the ACC a year ago, and it looks like this group will be better, but by how much?
 Sumler, Powell and Bethea appear to be the most promising options from the outside.  However, Bethea is a career 32% shooter from deep, Sumler's volume was not all that high from distance last season and Powell will be asked to play a much larger role than his previous two stops.
 There is also some competition to consider as well. The ACC went through a rough stretch for a couple of years where the perception of the conference was at an all-time low.  The league is still fighting that battle to a degree, but at the same time, many members of the league have upped their games.
 The ACC isn't the top-dog conference heading into the new season, but it's not pushover league either.  The Panthers will of course have to deal with the Duke and Carolinas of the world, but the rest of the league has taken steps forward, too and the league is slowly going through a revival after some down seasons.
 Perhaps above all else, it is also just hard to shake the overall recent lack of success for Pitt.  When you have a program that has just one tournament bid in the past nine years, there is obviously going to be some doubts about whether this it has turned the corner in such a short amount of time. 
 The portal can be a great equalizer and a way to make up ground quickly, but if your transfers do not gel the right way and things can go south in a hurry. This current set of Panthers may not own any of the prior stench cast on the program, but they'll carry a lot of the weight in trying to flip the script on the perception of it anyway.
 ONE PREDICTION 
 Pitt's defense gets a bounce back performance 
 The Miami Hurricanes had little trouble running all around the Pitt defense last week.  Miami torched Pitt for 503 yards, generated points on seven of its first eight possessions and came up with multiple big gains on third down conversions against the Panthers.
 It did not matter whether it was a short field or a long one, Miami  chipped away at the Panthers and made them look silly at times.  That of course followed a performance where Pitt allowed Boston College quarterback Mason McKenzie to throw for a career-high 295 yards the week prior.
 The scenarios were different and so were the breakdowns, but the fact of the matter is the Panthers simply haven't played good defense for a few weeks now and it's something that needs to change.
 It easy to recognize a good offense can help a defense, and that lack of symmetry has been a factor during this losing streak. At the same time, the Pitt defense welcomed the challenge and wanted to be a driving force while the offense was without its quarterback and this group hasn't done that yet.
 I think that can change tomorrow. The Panthers are due to get back on track on that side of the ball and they are facing a vulnerable opponent and it's imperative that they take advantage of that fact.
 Pitt's strong run defense should work well against a Georgia Tech team that has struggled to establish its ground game this season. Plus, the Panthers have the ability to be opportunistic against an offensive line that has had trouble blocking for its quarterback.
 The pass rush has been off and on this season, but the Panthers are now one of five ACC teams with 20 sacks this season and they're starting to become more effective in that department, largely fueled by the emergence of Jaeden Moore, who has four sacks in his past four games.
 Pitt is also second in the league with nine interceptions.  It may take some splash plays like a sack or a turnover  to come up with a win, but this is a team capable of having those moments. 
 The Panthers' downfall of late has been getting off the field on third downs.  Miami went 10-of-15 in such scenarios last week, but perhaps facing Georgia Tech could be what the doctored order for the defense.  The Yellow Jackets are ranked 114th in the country, picking up only 34% of their third-down chances this season.
 Pitt's notable defensive players, simply need to have big-time performances. The Panthers need their stars like Cruce Brookins, Braylan Lovelace and Nick James to rise up and make all-conference caliber plays and I think they will. I don't know if this will all result in a win for the Panthers, but I think at the very least the Pitt defense will do enough tomorrow to put the team in a position to come out on top.
